chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Duweyl, from Muqatil ibn Muqatil, who said:

I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'May I be sacrificed for you, teach me a supplication for fulfilling the needs.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'When you have an important need for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then perform Ghusl, wear your cleanest clothes, and smell some perfume. Then go out beneath the sky and pray two Rak'at. Commence the prayer by reciting Fatihat al-Kitab (the Opening of the Book) and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Say, He is Allah, One) fifteen times each.'
Then you bow (Ruku') and recite it fifteen times, then complete the prayer like the Prayer of Tasbih, except that the recitation is fifteen times. So when you give the Salam, recite it fifteen times.

Then you prostrate (Sajdah) and say in your prostration: 'O Allah, every worshipped entity from Your Throne to the settlement of Your earth is false except You, for You are Allah, the Evident Truth. Fulfill for me such and such a need. At this moment, at this moment,' and persist in what you desire.

key_terms.فَاتِحَةُ الْكِابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)
key_terms.قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ: Say, He is Allah, One (Surah Al-Ikhlas)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual procedure for the prayer of fulfilling needs according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith details a specific ritual prayer (Salat al-Hajah) prescribed by Imam Al-Reza (AS) for fulfilling urgent needs, emphasizing physical purification and spiritual focus. The practice involves performing Ghusl, wearing clean garments, and praying two Rak'at under the open sky, with repeated recitations of Surah Al-Fatiha and Surah Al-Ikhlas to affirm divine unity. The supplication concludes with a direct petition during prostration, highlighting the concept of 'Batil' (falsehood) of all other deities compared to Allah's absolute truth.
